# onetsolutions_hosting_php_version (Resource)

Manages the PHP version a domain of an OnetSolutions web hosting runs.

The web hosting must be active. Without `domain`, the resource sets the PHP version of the web
hosting's primary domain; `domain` can name any of its domains: subdomains and addon domains too.
`onetsolutions_hosting_php_versions` lists the versions offered and the version each domain runs.

-> **Destroying this resource sets the domain back to `inherit`**, the account's default PHP version.

A domain that inherits is listed with the version it runs, so with `php_version = "inherit"` the
state keeps `inherit`, and a version set outside Terraform afterwards is not detected. A domain
removed outside Terraform, or a web hosting that has ended, is forgotten by the next refresh.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "onetsolutions_hosting_php_versions" "site" {
  hosting_id = onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
}

# The primary domain of the web hosting.
resource "onetsolutions_hosting_php_version" "site" {
  hosting_id  = onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  php_version = "ea-php83"

  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = contains(data.onetsolutions_hosting_php_versions.site.versions[*].version, "ea-php83")
      error_message = "PHP 8.3 is not offered on this web hosting."
    }
  }
}

# Another domain of the same web hosting.
resource "onetsolutions_hosting_php_version" "legacy" {
  hosting_id  = onetsolutions_web_hosting.site.id
  domain      = "legacy.example.fr"
  php_version = "ea-php81"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `hosting_id` (String) The UUID of the web hosting. Changing it recreates the object in the other web hosting.
- `php_version` (String) The PHP version, as `onetsolutions_hosting_php_versions` lists it (such as `ea-php83`), or `inherit` for the account's default version. Checked at plan time against the versions the web hosting offers. Can be changed in place. With `inherit`, a version set outside Terraform afterwards is not detected.

### Optional

- `domain` (String) The domain of the web hosting, such as `blog.example.com`: its primary domain, a subdomain or an addon domain. When unset, the primary domain. Changing it targets another domain (replacement).
- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The domain, as `domain`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_hosting_php_version.site
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/4c3b2a1f-0e9d-4c8b-9a7f-6e5d4c3b2a1f/example.fr"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<hosting_id>/<domain>, or <hosting_id>/<domain> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_hosting_php_version.site 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/4c3b2a1f-0e9d-4c8b-9a7f-6e5d4c3b2a1f/example.fr
```
